rationales.decision: 60x45mm 2-layer board fed from a single 5V USB-C supply with a 500mA budget, so the golden task stays routable with the pinned Freerouting profile.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: left no routing headroom around the ESP32 antenna keepout
raises fabrication cost above the order budget cap for a demo board

assumptions.statement: Total load stays below the 500mA supplied by a USB-C sink with Rd termination.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

risks.description: The ESP32 antenna courtyard overhangs the board edge.
risks.mitigation: Antenna region is declared as a routing keepout and checked by DRC.

rationales.decision: USB-C receptacle as a 5V sink with 5.1k Rd on both CC pins and a 10uF bulk capacitor.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: obsolete connector and no CC-based current negotiation

assumptions.statement: A 5.1k Rd on each CC pin advertises the default USB Type-C sink current.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

rationales.decision: AMS1117-3.3 linear regulator with 10uF input and 22uF output bulk capacitance.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: adds SI and EMC verification beyond the Phase 2 boundary
the datasheet requires output bulk capacitance for stability

assumptions.statement: Regulator dropout is acceptable because the ESP32 peak current is supplied from bulk capacitance.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

risks.description: Linear regulation dissipates the 5V to 3.3V difference as heat.
risks.mitigation: SOT-223 package with copper pour; thermal analysis is out of the Phase 2 scope.

rationales.decision: ESP32-WROOM-32E module with 100nF decoupling on each supply pin, so RF and firmware qualification stay inside the module vendor's scope.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: requires RF matching and certification work outside Phase 2
leaves supply transients unbounded at the module pins

assumptions.statement: Module-level certification covers the RF section, so the board only supplies power and IO.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

rationales.decision: BME280 on I2C with 4.7k pull-ups on SDA and SCL and SDO tied low through 10k to fix the address.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: ESP32 and BME280 do not provide I2C bus pull-ups, so the bus would not settle
uses more IO than the header budget allows

assumptions.statement: 4.7k pull-ups keep the bus inside the 1k-10k window at 100kHz standard mode.
Bus rise time meets the I2C specification with the assembled trace capacitance.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

rationales.decision: 2.54mm 1x06 header exposing UART, 3V3 and GND for bring-up and flashing.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: adds a component and firmware dependency not needed for the golden task
cannot be probed with a standard serial cable during bring-up

assumptions.statement: An external USB-UART adapter supplies the flashing signals.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

rationales.decision: Single red status LED driven from 3V3 through a 330 ohm series resistor, about 3.9mA.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: exceeds the LED forward current rating
drives about 59mA and destroys the LED

assumptions.statement: 3.9mA is visible enough for a status indicator in indoor light.

provenance.pendingReason: rationale is fixture-owned and is not verification evidence

rationales.decision: EN and IO0 pulled up through 10k with tactile switches to ground for reset and download mode.

alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: requires the USB-UART bridge that this board does not carry
leaves the strapping pins floating and the boot mode undefined

assumptions.statement: 10k pull-ups hold the strapping pins high while the switches pull them low.
